nca_vs_original.gif: Frames 1850-2029 (every 2nd frame), the same stretch as the README preview. Left: the original as a 48x36 black-and-white grid. Right: a replay of the saved full-song model (runs/featured/whole_song_s0.ncab) started from frame 0, with no frames fed in. The model uses 110 learned rules on a fixed timeline and only reproduces this one video.
nca_state.gif: Inside the full-song model, frames 1850-1939: the visible pixel layer and 3 of the 15 hidden layers (each scaled to its own range over the clip). Replayed from runs/featured/whole_song_s0.ncab starting at frame 0; the rule in use switches at fixed frames.
fantasmagorie_nca.gif: The same kind of model trained from scratch on Fantasmagorie (Emile Cohl, 1908, public domain), replayed from runs/gen/fit/fa_full/model.ncab. It reproduces this film only; it was not transferred from the Bad Apple model.
logic_gh_9gates.gif: A rule made of 9 logic gates, learned from examples and then simplified, running from a random start (ui/static/logic_examples/greenberg_hastings.logic.json). Yellow = excited, blue = recovering. It matches the known excitable-wave rule on all 262,144 possible neighbourhoods. This is a known synthetic rule, not one found in Bad Apple.
logic_realvideo_failure.gif: A learned logic-gate rule on real Bad Apple frames (ui/static/logic_examples/d4_G_s0_b144k.logic.json), started at frame 3996 and then left to run. It keeps the silhouette for a few frames and then grows it into a blob. Left: the original 48x36 frames.
shape_ring.gif: Synthetic test: squashing a thin ring (runs/shape/synth_preds.npz). All three rules are hand-written and steered by controls chosen while looking at the intended frames. Shifting regions independently tears the ring; a smooth field from 9 control points keeps it connected (that field is computed from points far away, so it is not a purely local rule).
